findings.summary: For reviewer == 'plan-reviewer', assignment_scope is set to current_artifacts, which is built from bundle['plan_path'] / bundle['spec_path'] (lines 209-213). But two of the plan's deliverable contracts diverge from the design it declares as its evidence base: the corpus acceptance criterion imports Cut 3's replay column (PRB4-01) and the redaction contract drops the finding ids the design specifies keeping (PRB4-03).

The architecture is sound — per-(change,reviewer) counting is the correct answer to plan_ready re-firing via transitions.py:37, epochs are correctly left anchoring contract freezing, and the close-ordering carve-out in Task 5 is right. Two pinned behaviours are internally inconsistent: PRB4-02 (a round the design calls locally decreasing is pinned as 'no improvement') and PRB4-04 (per-role defaults with no stated fallback for the arbitrary role keys the loader accepts).

Verified by sweeping all files matching max_automatic_rounds_per_epoch|automatic_rounds_used (26 files; the sole undeclared one, tests/unit/cli/test_review_human.py:197, touches only automatic_rounds_used, whose meaning the plan preserves) and by checking that the new event type breaks no undeclared test: tests/unit/core/test_events.py and test_transitions.py use subset assertions, and test_gen_state_machine.py derives NOOP_EVENTS from _INFORMATIONAL with a tolerant row-count range.

findings.summary: Task 3's corpus acceptance criterion and the matching 'Done when' clause (line 218) state that at a budget of 6 'the six converging changes require zero' authorizations and the corpus 'authorizes only on the two changes that diverged'. That is the design document's 'threshold + budget' column (11 prompts, only stage5b and stage1), and the severity threshold is Cut 3, explicitly out of scope here (line 66). Cut 1 alone is the 'budget alone' column: 26 prompts. Recomputing from the design's own per-change curves at a per-change budget of 6 — stage3a 9 rounds -> 3, stage3b 18 -> 12, stage1 13 -> 7, stage5b 10 -> 4 — gives exactly the 26 in that cell, spread over four changes including two the design classifies as converged. An implementer writing this test gets 26 authorizations over 4 changes and must either fail the criterion or bend the counter to make it pass.

Task 4's headline case is self-contradictory. It pins 'corpus-06 at round 7 reports the curve [3,2,3,2,2,1], no improvement'. On that curve the last completed round produced 1 blocker+major against the previous round's 2 — an improvement under the only metric the curve supplies. The design confirms it: it says stage5b (corpus-06 per Task 1 line 94) defeats a three-rounds-without-improvement rule precisely because rounds 4-6 are 'locally decreasing'. Either the pinned expectation is wrong or 'improved' is measured on the total-findings curve rather than the blocker+major curve, which the plan never says; the implementer cannot write this test without guessing.
